oneLiner: Continue Codex Widget for Desktop through vibe-iterate and close the remaining feasible backlog.
inferredDomain: Resident Windows desktop AI agent widget with daemon-owned local state, Codex app-server runtime sessions, provider history, Vision sharing, PTY, artifacts, and dogfooding readiness.

coverage.goal: Close durable runtime/session correctness, provider snapshot history UI, Vision resource tuning, and completion audit.
coverage.target_user: Primary user is the desktop dogfooder/developer who keeps the Codex Widget resident and expects persistent sessions, local file/tool access, and reliable UI state.
coverage.platform: Windows Tauri shell, React renderer, Node daemon, local WebSocket protocol, SQLite metadata store, file-backed blob store.
coverage.data_model: Sessions, messages, runtime threads, provider snapshots, Vision streams, artifacts, activity logs, themes, mascots, and module metadata are daemon-owned.
coverage.primary_interaction: The user switches internal chat tabs, restores sessions, branches responses, captures/shares screen context, uses PTY, and expects Agent turns to preserve the intended session context.
coverage.success_metric: Smoke gates pass and durable state records which backlog items are implemented, deferred, or dogfood-dependent.
coverage.constraints: Do not persist OAuth/Codex credentials. Redact large provider/image payloads. Keep app-server protocol fallback-safe because it is experimental.
coverage.tech_stack: TypeScript, React, Tauri, Node daemon, SQLite, WebSocket, Codex app-server with exec fallback.

carryoverSummary: Iteration 4 completed the visible UI/context/artifact/Vision/PTX polish set. The remaining feasible backlog is runtime thread rebinding, provider history visibility, Vision resource tuning, and a final audit.
